info.title: Whalesync API
info.description: Create and monitor Whalesync syncs. Everything under `/v1/sync/…` is the sync feature; other Whalesync features will get their own prefix. Authenticate every request with an API key from Settings > API keys: `Authorization: Bearer ws_tok_…`. All fields are snake_case (credential field ids inside `auth` are the exception: they are the ids the connector registry declares, e.g. Postgres's `connectionString`). List endpoints take `limit` and `cursor` and return `{data, has_more, next_cursor}`. Every authenticated response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` headers (one per-key budget); a `429` adds `Retry-After`. Errors that need a person first come back `409` with `type: requires_action` and a `required_action` object — relay its `instruction` and `url` to a human.

post.description: Creates a sync with both sides declared inline. API-key connectors can take their credentials in `auth`, validated live against the connected service; `base` resolves by remote id or exact display name. Any side declared by connector alone — an OAuth side always, an API-key side whenever credentials should not pass through the caller — is left for a person, who connects it in the app via the returned pending action. A `201` means everything sent was validated — on any error, nothing is kept.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes retries safe: the same key replays the original response instead of creating twice.

201.description: The new sync, in `draft`. A side left for a person — OAuth, or API-key without `auth` — comes back `null` with a `user_authorization` entry in `pending_actions`.

400.description: Nothing was created: `unknown_connector`, `invalid_auth` (credentials failed the live check), `missing_auth`/`missing_base` (an API-key side sent only one of `auth`/`base` — send both, or neither to leave the side for a person), `auth_not_supported`/`base_not_supported` on an OAuth side, `base_not_found`/`base_ambiguous` (with the reachable bases in `details.bases`), or `idempotency_key_reused` (same `Idempotency-Key`, different body).

put.description: Full replace: anything omitted is unmapped, omitted settings revert to defaults — fetch-modify-put is the intended editing pattern. `{"create": {"name": "…"}}` placeholders create the table/field on that side, typed from the mapped counterpart; retries safely adopt already-created objects. Referenced tables whose fields were never fetched are fetched during the call, so a first PUT can take a few seconds. Any change returns the sync to `draft` for a human to review and start. The read-only `filter` and `advanced_settings` a GET reports are ignored here and keep their stored values — they are edited in the app.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The revision the edit was based on; `412` on mismatch.

200.description: The resolved document, with created objects under their real remote ids.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when this is a stored replay of an earlier identical request.

400.description: The document is invalid: a structural problem or unknown reference names its JSON-pointer `path` in the message (`unknown_table`, `unknown_field`, `table_ambiguous`, `view_required`, `view_not_found`, `view_not_supported`); `invalid_mappings` carries the per-field problems in `details.issues`; a `create` that the connector refused is `create_failed`; a mapped table the connector could not prepare for syncing (some add a Whalesync ID column first) is `table_setup_failed`; an `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different body is `idempotency_key_reused`.

post.description: The authoritative compatibility check: field type compatibility, required and orphaned fields, linked-record constraints, create-placeholder feasibility, and everything the mappings PUT would enforce — as one issue list with stable codes and document paths. Side-effect-free: `create` placeholders are checked, never executed. Send a candidate document, or an empty body to validate the stored one. Referenced tables whose fields were never fetched are fetched during the call, so a first validate can take a few seconds. Two failure channels: a structurally malformed document (wrong types, bad `direction`, a create on both sides) is a `400 invalid_mappings` naming the path — everything semantic about a well-formed document comes back as a `200` with issues.

200.description: The issues found; empty means valid.

400.description: The candidate document is structurally malformed (`invalid_mappings`, with the path).

get.description: One sync's deletes waiting on a person, newest first. When a record goes missing on one side, Whalesync holds the delete instead of applying it to the other side, so an accidental or API-caused disappearance cannot destroy data. Approving or ignoring a delete is deliberately not in this API: it is irreversible, so it stays a decision a person makes in the app — relay `review_url`.

post.description: Create the mapped tables and fields in the destination, then apply the runnable pipeline — as one background job. This is the apply point: mapping edits change nothing until a save lands. Poll `GET …/save` until `succeeded` (which also means `unsaved_changes` is false on the export — the authoritative confirmation), then set the schedule or trigger a run. Single-flight and per-item retryable: POST again after a failure and everything already created is skipped. This writes to the destination app.

action.description: What to do with `url`: open it in a browser. It is a page for a person, never an endpoint to call.

type.description: How to handle the failure, independent of the HTTP status. `requires_action` means a person has to do something first and always carries `required_action`; everything wrong with the request itself — malformed, unknown resource, or a state the resource is not in — is `invalid_request_error`.

code.description: Stable identifier for this failure. Branch on this, never on the message.

required_action.description: The step a person has to take in the browser before this call can succeed — the same object as the sync's `pending_actions` entries. Relay its `instruction` and `url` to a human. Present on every `requires_action` error, and on the two `authentication_error` codes, where it points at creating a key.

details.description: Machine-readable extras for codes that carry them (e.g. the candidate bases on `base_ambiguous`).

name.description: The base name as shown by the connector.

url.description: A link to open the base in its own service, if any.

left.description: The left side, or null while unset.

right.description: The right side, or null while unset.

mappings_revision.description: Opaque revision of the mappings document; changes on every mappings edit. Doubles as the mappings ETag — compare it across polls to detect edits made in the app during a handoff.

open_issues.description: Unresolved issues across both sides. Read the detail from `GET /v1/sync/issues?sync=…`.

delete_approval.description: `review_required` means a record that goes missing on one side waits for a person to approve the delete before it is applied to the other side; `auto_approve` means deletes are applied as soon as they are detected, and there is no queue to read.

pending_deletes.description: Deletes waiting on a person right now. Always 0 under `auto_approve`, where nothing waits. Read the detail from `GET /v1/sync/pending-deletes?sync=…`.

initial_sync_running.description: Whether the initial sync is running: the first match and copy of records between the two apps, started when a person activates the sync. `status` is `paused` until it finishes and the sync turns on.

last_synced_at.description: When the sync last polled, or null if never.

review_url.description: The sync's page in the app, where a human reviews the mappings and starts it.

pending_actions.description: What a person still has to do in the browser before this sync can run: connect a side whose app signs in there, then review and start it. Empty when nothing is waiting on anyone. Agents cannot perform these — relay the `instruction` and `url`.

schedule.description: Null until the first save provisions the pipeline.

unsaved_changes.description: True when mappings were edited over the API after the last save — `trigger` would run the last-applied pipeline, not the edits. Save to clear it. (An edit saved in the app clears it on the next save poll.)

app_url.description: The export in the Whalesync app — a convenience link, never a required step (anything that needs a person arrives as a pending action).

mappings_url.description: The working mappings document — edit, then save.

save_url.description: The save saga: POST to apply the mappings, GET to poll.

runs_url.description: The run history, pre-filtered to this export.

has_more.description: Whether more live exports follow this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

auth.description: Credential fields for an `api_key` connector, keyed by the field ids from `GET /v1/live-export/connectors`. Never returned by any endpoint. Completes a side that was created without credentials.

location.description: Destination side only: where created tables live (an id from `GET …/destination/locations`, e.g. a Notion parent page). Only needed for destinations that host tables somewhere pickable.

enabled.description: Whether the cadence is on. This is the on/off switch for the whole export.

cron.description: The exact schedule, as a cron expression. Read-only; set `cadence` instead.

next_run_at.description: When the next scheduled run fires.

allowed_cadences.description: The cadences your plan can set. Pick from these to avoid a `plan_required` error.

enabled.description: The on/off switch for the whole export. `trigger` still works while off.

cadence.description: How often scheduled runs fire. Cadences above your plan are rejected — see `allowed_cadences`.

force.description: Run even though the mappings have unsaved edits (the run uses the last-saved pipeline, not them). Without it, that state is the `unsaved_changes` conflict.

action.description: What the step does to your data. `write` is the step that changes the destination.

trigger.description: Whether a person/API started it, or the cadence did.

summary.description: The one-line story: what the run is doing right now, or how it ended.

warning.description: Set when the run completed but a step finished with a warning.

error.description: The rolled-up error for a failed run.

app_url.description: The run in the Whalesync app, for a person who wants to watch or share it — like every app_url, nothing here needs their attention.

live_export_id.description: The Live Export this run belongs to.

steps.description: The ordered phases of the run. Detail reads only.

running.description: Whether a run is in flight right now — independent of the schedule.

next_run_at.description: When the next scheduled run fires.

id.description: The id to use as `source_table` in the mappings document.
The id to use as `source_field` in the mappings document.

name.description: The destination column name the server suggests.

type.description: The destination type the server planned. When the source and destination are the same kind of database, this is the destination's exact column type (e.g. `text[]`, `numeric(12,2)`). Otherwise it's one of `text`, `longText`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `select`, `multiSelect`, `url`, `email`, `phone`, `currency` or `json`, with ` list` appended for a field that holds several values (e.g. `text list`). Informational — not settable.

suggested_primary.description: True for the server's suggested primary (title) field, when the destination needs one.

source_record_id.description: True for the source-record-id field — how re-runs update a record instead of duplicating it. Always included in created tables, picked or not.

has_more.description: True when the destination has more locations than it returns — pass `?search=` to find one.

revision.description: Compare-and-set token for PUT (also sent as the `ETag` header).

tables.description: The document is {"tables": [{"source_table", "destination_table": {"create": {"name"}}, "fields": [{"source_field", "destination_field": {"create": {"name", "primary?"}}}]}]}. Reference source tables and fields by the ids the discovery endpoints return; destination tables and fields are created by the export, so they take names, never types — types come from the plan behind …/fields.

message.description: What is wrong, in caller terms.

path.description: Where in the document, when it is one place.

valid.description: True when a PUT of this document would be accepted.

name.description: The table or field that failed, by name.

phase.description: What the save is doing: creating destination tables/fields, then applying the pipeline.

errors.description: Per-item failures. Fix and POST again.

message.description: The state as one human sentence, ready to show to a person.

has_more.description: Whether more retained runs follow this page.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

source.description: Usable as the app records are read from.

destination.description: Usable as the app tables are written into.

id.description: The key to use for this field inside `auth`.

optional.description: Whether the field may be omitted.

placeholder.description: Example or hint text for the value.

method.description: `oauth` connects in the browser (a person signs in; the export carries a pending action). `api_key` may also take `auth` inline at create.

fields.description: The credential fields for `api_key` connectors; null for `oauth`.

type.description: The slug to pass as a side's `connector`.

available.description: False when the connector needs a higher plan (see `required_plan`).

required_plan.description: The plan that unlocks it, when `available` is false.
